sources.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
sources.venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, 3(4):333-389

establishes.statement: Formalizes BM25, the bag-of-words token-matching retrieval function used as the field's standard lexical baseline.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [55] for BM25, used throughout Sections 1, 2.1 and 4
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [55]; cited at lines 9, 133-134, 357

sources.why_useful: Grounds the BM25 baseline central to the paper's headline finding.

sources.title: Bridging the lexical chasm: statistical approaches to answer-finding
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd annual international ACM SIGIR conference on Research and development in information retrieval, pages 192-199

establishes.statement: Names and studies the 'lexical gap': lexical retrieval systems can only match documents that share surface keywords with the query.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [5] for the 'lexical gap', motivating why lexical approaches are limited
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [5]; cited at lines 9, 134

sources.why_useful: Motivates why neural retrieval was pursued at all, needed for adjacent-ML background.

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

establishes.statement: Introduces BERT, the pre-trained Transformer encoder underlying nearly every neural retriever evaluated in this paper.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [13] (NAACL version) / [12] (arXiv preprint version) for BERT
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entries [12]-[13]; cited at lines 10, 133

sources.why_useful: Background the adjacent-ML audience already has, but needed as the shared foundation model referenced by DPR/ANCE/TAS-B/DeepCT/SPARTA/BM25+CE.

sources.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

establishes.statement: Introduces DPR, a dense bi-encoder passage retriever trained with BM25 hard negatives and in-batch negatives.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [31] for DPR, described and evaluated as one of the 10 BEIR systems
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [31]; cited at lines 134, 361

sources.why_useful: Source of the DPR baseline, the worst zero-shot generalizer in the results.

sources.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval
sources.venue: (as cited in project/paper.txt reference list; venue not further specified there)

establishes.statement: Introduces ANCE, a dense bi-encoder trained with hard negatives mined from an approximate nearest-neighbor index updated during training.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [73] for ANCE, described and evaluated as one of the 10 BEIR systems
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [73]; cited at lines 134, 361, 703

sources.why_useful: Source of the ANCE baseline, used throughout the length-preference and TAS-B comparisons.

sources.title: Efficiently Teaching an Effective Dense Retriever with Balanced Topic Aware Sampling

establishes.statement: Introduces TAS-B, a dense bi-encoder trained with Balanced Topic-Aware Sampling and a combination of Margin-MSE and in-batch-negative losses distilled from a cross-encoder/ColBERT ensemble.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [23] for TAS-B, the best-generalizing dense model evaluated
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [23]; cited at line 361

sources.why_useful: Source of the TAS-B baseline, the best-generalizing dense model in the results.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International ACM SIGIR Conference, pages 39-48

establishes.statement: Introduces ColBERT, a late-interaction architecture that computes token-level contextualized embeddings and aggregates similarity with a max-similarity operation.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [32] for ColBERT, described and evaluated as one of the 10 BEIR systems
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [32]; cited at lines 134, 362

sources.why_useful: Source of the late-interaction architecture family, one of the two best zero-shot generalizers.

sources.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT

establishes.statement: Shows that a cross-attentional BERT-based re-ranker applied to a first-stage retriever's candidates substantially improves ranking quality, at added computational cost.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [46] for BERT-based re-ranking
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [46]; cited at lines 10, 135

sources.why_useful: Establishes the cross-encoder re-ranking family instantiated as BM25+CE, the best zero-shot generalizer overall.

sources.title: Document Expansion by Query Prediction
sources.venue: (as cited in project/paper.txt reference list; venue not further specified there)

establishes.statement: Introduces document expansion by predicting queries a document could answer and appending them for lexical search (the basis for docT5query).
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [48] for document expansion, the technique behind docT5query
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [48]; cited at line 134

sources.why_useful: Source of docT5query, a sparse method that generalizes unusually well for a sparse architecture.

sources.title: MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation for Task-Agnostic Compression of Pre-Trained Transformers
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 33, pages 5776-5788

establishes.statement: Introduces MiniLM, a small distilled Transformer used as the cross-encoder in the BM25+CE re-ranking system.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [70] for the MiniLM cross-encoder used in BM25+CE
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [70]; cited at line 363

sources.why_useful: Identifies the specific cross-encoder model behind the best-generalizing system.

sources.title: MultiReQA: A Cross-Domain Evaluation for Retrieval Question Answering Models
sources.venue: (as cited in project/paper.txt reference list; venue not further specified there)

establishes.statement: MultiReQA evaluates sentence-level answer retrieval across eight QA datasets, five of which are Wikipedia-based, over comparatively small corpora.
establishes.support_quote: 'It only tests a single task and five out of eight datasets are from Wikipedia. Further, MultiReQA evaluates retrieval over rather small corpora: six out of eight tasks have less than 100k candidate sentences.'

sources.why_useful: Prior multi-dataset benchmark motivating the GAP: a single task, mostly small Wikipedia corpora.
sources.limitations: Read only via project/paper.txt's own characterization; the original abstract was not independently retrieved (no web access in this run).

sources.title: KILT: a Benchmark for Knowledge Intensive Language Tasks
sources.venue: (as cited in project/paper.txt reference list; venue not further specified there)

establishes.statement: KILT covers five knowledge-intensive task types over eleven datasets, but retrieves documents only from Wikipedia and treats retrieval as a supporting step rather than the primary task.
establishes.support_quote: 'KILT consists of five knowledge-intensive tasks including a total of eleven datasets. The tasks involve retrieval, but it is not the primary task. Further, KILT retrieves documents only from Wikipedia.'

sources.why_useful: Second prior multi-dataset benchmark motivating the GAP: retrieval is secondary and Wikipedia-only.
sources.limitations: Read only via project/paper.txt's own characterization; the original abstract was not independently retrieved (no web access in this run).

sources.title: TREC-COVID: Constructing a Pandemic Information Retrieval Test Collection

establishes.statement: Constructs the TREC-COVID test collection using a multi-system pooling method, the collection later used for the annotation-bias case study.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [65] for TREC-COVID; 'TREC-COVID used a pooling method to reduce the impact of the aforementioned bias: The annotation set was constructed by using the search results from the various systems participating in the challenge.'
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [65]; described at lines 123, 703

sources.why_useful: Source of the dataset used for the annotation-bias case study central to the paper's third finding.

sources.title: Resources for Brewing BEIR: Reproducible Reference Models and Statistical Analyses
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 47th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '24), pages 1431-1440

establishes.statement: A later resource paper reports that comparisons on BEIR, formed by averaging scores across heterogeneous datasets into one number, are difficult to interpret, and provides reproducible reference implementations and effect-size meta-analyses to address this.
establishes.support_quote: 'comparisons on BEIR are performed by reducing scores from heterogeneous datasets into a single average that is difficult to interpret. To remedy this, we present meta-analyses focusing on effect sizes across datasets that are able to accurately quantify model differences.'

sources.why_useful: Directly relevant follow-up caveat on the averaging methodology used for this paper's own headline comparison (C006); cited in the Discussion/Limitations.

sources.title: MS MARCO: A Human Generated MAchine Reading COmprehension Dataset
sources.venue: (as cited in project/paper.txt reference list; venue not further specified there)

establishes.statement: Introduces MS MARCO, the large passage-ranking dataset used to fine-tune the majority of the retrievers evaluated in this paper and to report their in-domain scores.
establishes.support_quote: cited in project/paper.txt as reference [45] for MS MARCO, used for training/in-domain evaluation throughout Sections 1, 3 and 4
establishes.location: project/paper.txt reference list, entry [45]; cited at lines 10, 138, 158, 839

sources.why_useful: Source of the training/in-domain dataset central to the paper's headline in-domain-vs-zero-shot comparison.
